answer.evidence: The stair block (rows 0-31) is four repeated 8-row steps. Each step has a light highlight at its top (rows 0-2, 8, 16, 24) and 3-5 rows of mid-grey stone below it. Each step ends in a dark shadow band (rows 5-7, 14-15, 22-23, 30-31) that reads as eave shadow under the tread's front edge, with the riser face below. The tread/riser split is ambiguous because the highlight sits at the top of each step rather than at its front edge. I read the highlight plus mid-grey stone as a tread seen from above, and the dark band as the riser shadow. There is no receding side face. Rows 32-47 are a flat cobblestone floor at the cliff foot.
